Eco-Resort Management Practices

Ecotourism is often a.s a form Of nature-based tourism and has an immyrtant alternative source of tourists. In addition to providing the traditional resort-leisure product, it has Ixen argued that ecotourism resort management should have a particular f'Rus on best-practice environmental management. an educational and interpretive component, and direct and indirect contributions to the conservation of the natural and cultural envirotunent (Ayala, 1996). Couran Cove Island Resort is a large integrated •xotourism-based resort located south of Brisbane on the Gold Coast. Queensland, Australia. As the world's population becomes increasingly urbanised. the demand for tourist attractions which are environmentally friendly. serene and Offer amenities of a unique nature has grown rapidly. Couran Cove Resort, which is one such tourist attractions, is on South Stradbroke Island. crcupying approximately 150 hectares of the island. South Stradbroke Island is separated from the mainland by the Broadwater, a stretch of sea 3 kilometres wide. More than a century ago, there was only one Stradbroke Island. and there were at least four Atoriginal tribes living and hunting on the island. Regrettably, most Of the original island dwellers were eventually killed by diseases such as tuberculosis. smallpox and influenzÆ by the end Of the 19th century. The ship wrecked on the island in 1894. and the subsequent destruction of the ship (the Cambus Wallace) because it contained dynamite, caused a large crater in the sandhills on Stradbroke Island. Eventually, the ocean broke through the weakened land form and Stradbroke Excarne two islands. Couran Cove Island Resort is built on one of the world's few naturally-CK'curring sand lands, which is home to a wide range of plant communities and one of the largest remaining remnants of the rare livistona rainforest left on the Gold Coast. Many mangrove and rainforest areas, and Malaleuc.a Wetlands On South Stradbroke Island (and in Queensland), have txen cleared. drairi«l or filled for residential. industrial, agricultural or urban development in the first half of the 20th century. Farmers and graziers finally abandoned South Stradbroke Island in 1939 the vegetation and the soil conditions there were not suitable for agricultural activities.

SUSTAINABLE PRACTICES OF COURAN COVE RESORT

Being lcxated on an offshore island, the resort is only accessible by means Of water transport. The resort provides hourly ferry service from the marina on the mainland to and from the island. Within the resort. transport modes include walking trails, bicycle tracks and the train. The reception area is the counter of the shop which has not changed for S years at least. As an ecotourism-lwed resort, most of the planning and development of the attraction has concenon the need to co-exist with the fragile natural environment of South Stradbroke Island to achieve sustainable development.

WATER AND ENERGY MANAGEMENT

South Stradbroke Island has groundwater at the centre of the island, which has a maximum height of 3 metres atove sea level. The water supply is by rainfall and is commonly known as an unconfined freshwater aquifer. Couran Cove Island Resort obtains its water supply by tapping into this aquifer and extracting it via a l.x»re system. Some of the problems which have threatened the island's freshwater supply include 'X)llution, contamination and over-consumption. In order to minimise some of these problems, all laundry activities are out on the mainland. The resort considers washing machines as onerous to the island's freshwater supply. and that the detergents contain a high level of phosphates which are a major of water pollution. The resort uses LPG-JV)wer generation rather than a dieselvowered plant for its energy supply. supplemented by wind turbine, which has reduced greenhouse emissions by 70% of diesel-equivalent generation meth€xls. Excess heat recovered from the generator is used to heat the swimming Hot water in the eco-cabins and for some of the resort's vehicles are solarpowered. Water efficient fittings are installed in showers and toilets. However, not all the appliances used by the resort are energy efficient. such as refrigerators. Visitors who stay at the resort are encouraged to monitor their water and energy usage via the in-house television systems, and are rewarded with prizes (such as a free return trip to the resort) accordingly if their usage level is low.

CONCLUDING REMARKS

We examined a case study of good management practice and a pro-active sustainable tourism stance of an eco-resolt. In three years Of operation, Couran Cove Island Resort has won 23 international and national awards, including the 2CÅ)l Australian Tourism Award in the 4-Star Accomnuxlation category. The resort has embraced and has effectively implemented contemporary environmental management practices. It has argued that the successful implementation of the principles of sustainability should promote longterm scrial. and environmental while ensuring and enhancing the prosrrcts of continued viability for the tourism entemrise. Couran Cove Island Reson docs m.»t conform to the characteristics of tiw• Resort Developtnent Spectrum. as protxvsed by Prideaux According to Prideaux, the resort should at least at Phase 3 of the model (the National tourism phase), which an integrated resort providing 3-4 star hotel-tyiX accommcxiation. lhe primary tourist market in Phase 3 of the Iruniel consists mainly of interstate visitors. However. the of interstate and international tourists visiting the resort is small, with the principal visitor markets comprising locals and residents from nearby towns and the Gold Coast region. The carrying capacity Of Couran Cove seem to bc of any concem to the Resort management. Given that it is a private commercial ecotourist enterprise, regulating the of visitors to the resort to minimise damage done to the natural environment on South Stradbroke Island is not a binding constraint. However. the Resort's growth will eventually constrained by its carrying carvwity, and quantity control should incorrorated in the management strategy of the resort.

Mark Turin, a university professor. has launched WOLP (World Oral Language Project) to prevent the language from the brink Of extinction.
